subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in `config validate`/doctor, hard validation errors, or left to startup/runtime handling when catalog authority is incomplete?
rationale: The source seam is clear, but the behavior affects custom providers, user-declared catalog rows, forward-compatible model names, fail-closed validation, and upgrade safety, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed warnings in `config validate` and doctor, with wording that distinguishes trusted catalog misses from custom or forward-compatible setups.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs at validation time, accepting a compatibility break unless an explicit escape or custom-provider contract is added.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on startup/runtime errors plus fallback notices instead of adding a new config analyzer.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed warnings in `config validate` and doctor, with wording that distinguishes trusted catalog misses from custom or forward-compatible setups.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest observed history on the shared model-selection and compatibility boundary that the policy decision must preserve.
